title: Labrador City Home Rebates 2026: NL Hydro, Oil to Heat Pump, Insulation
desc: Labrador City home rebates for 2026: takeCHARGE programs for NL Hydro customers, Oil to Electric up to $22,000, insulation for 1960s and 70s homes, and what to confirm first.
lead: Labrador City gets its power from NL Hydro, not Newfoundland Power, and most of its homes were built in the 1960s and 70s mining boom. The takeCHARGE rebates are open to NL Hydro customers too. Here is what is open on October 16, 2026 and the one thing to confirm before you start.
cards_heading: What is open in Labrador City in 2026
cards_intro: We read the takeCHARGE and Government of Newfoundland and Labrador pages on October 16, 2026. Each card links to its source.

cards.title: Heat pump (switching from oil)
cards.note: Oil or propane homes on the interconnected grid (confirm with Hydro), income-qualified. Up to $9,000 for others.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: 75% of the cost for attic and basement, plus labour. Electric heat, home built before 2014.

cards.title: Air sealing
cards.note: Based on blower door results. Electric heat and an HRV or air exchanger needed.

cards.title: HRV
cards.note: Eligible model, HRAI certified installer, any heat source.

cards.title: No-cost upgrades
cards.note: TakeCharge Greener Homes Program for income-qualified homeowners.

cards.title: Oil heating supplement
cards.note: Bought 250 litres of oil in 2026, family income $150,000 or less. Apply by January 15, 2027.

sections: What Labrador City homes look like

The 2021 Census counted 3,070 households in Labrador City. About 77% of homes were built between 1961 and 1980, and about 83% before 1981, the highest share of the places we cover in the province. About 78% of households own their home. The housing mix is different from the island cities: few duplex units, more semi-detached homes (about 16%) and row houses (about 11%), and about 8% movable dwellings such as mobile homes.

Source: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census, table 98-10-0233-01.

Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro serves Labrador City and Wabush, with power coming over transmission lines from Churchill Falls. takeCHARGE is run by Hydro and Newfoundland Power together, so Hydro customers can apply for the same rebates. For takeCHARGE questions, Hydro's line is 1-888-737-1296.
Confirm your grid before Oil to Electric

Oil to Electric needs your home to be connected to the island grid or Labrador's interconnected grid. Labrador City is fed from Churchill Falls, but the program page does not list communities, so call Hydro to confirm your home qualifies before you get quotes. If it does, a central heat pump can get up to $22,000 when your household is income-qualified (for example $131,100 or less for four), or up to $9,000 if not. Western Labrador winters are long and cold, so pay attention to the backup heat the program requires.

A home from the 1960s or 70s often has less insulation than today's code. With electric heat, takeCHARGE pays 75% of the insulation cost, up to $1,000 for the attic and $1,000 for the basement, plus up to $500 each for labour by a participating installer, and $200 to $750 for air sealing with blower door tests. Ask Hydro whether participating installers travel to Labrador West.

The rebates need a home on a permanent foundation. If you live in a mobile home, ask takeCHARGE whether yours counts before you plan around a rebate. Income-qualified homeowners can apply to the TakeCharge Greener Homes Program for no-cost upgrades after a home energy assessment. It is separate from the old federal Canada Greener Homes Grant, which has ended.
claim_steps: Call NL Hydro (1-888-737-1296) to confirm which programs your home qualifies for.
Lower income: apply to TakeCharge Greener Homes first.
Electric heat: ask about participating insulation installers who serve Labrador West.
Oil heat: apply for the Home Heating Supplement, then get Oil to Electric quotes.
faq: Can NL Hydro customers get takeCHARGE rebates?
Yes. takeCHARGE is run by NL Hydro and Newfoundland Power, and its programs list customers of either utility.
Does Labrador City qualify for Oil to Electric?
The program covers homes on the island or Labrador interconnected grid. Labrador City is supplied from Churchill Falls, but confirm with Hydro at 1-888-737-1296 before you get quotes.
Can I get a rebate for a mobile home?
The rebates require a permanent foundation. Ask takeCHARGE whether your home counts.
Is there a heat pump rebate for homes with electric heat?
We found no takeCHARGE heat pump rebate for homes already on electric heat. Hydro offers on-bill financing for heat pumps.
